summary: Theo Murray works in Buddhist and religious studies. Murray is a PhD student and candidate at the Australian National University (attested 2026).

Theodoor Paul Galestin was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed his PhD at Leiden University (1927–1936) under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. He was an extraordinary professor at the University of Amsterdam (1945–1957) and professor at Leiden University (1957–1977).

Theodor Aufrecht was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and earned his PhD at the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Berlin, the Bodleian Library, the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875), and the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Baader worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Bern and earned his PhD at the University of Münster (1910–1913), where he became Privatdozent in 1920, later serving as professor at Radboud University Nijmegen (1923–1944).

Theodor Baunack was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Georg Curtius and Hermann Brockhaus at the University of Leipzig, completed his PhD at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and taught at the Alte Nikolaischule from 1889.

Theodor Benfey was an Indologist and linguist who completed his education, PhD, and habilitation at the University of Göttingen. He spent his career there as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and ordinarius professor (1862–1881).

Theodor Bloch was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned his PhD at Leipzig and habilitated there in 1896. He later served as Superintendent of the Eastern Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1900) and Reader at the University of Calcutta (~1908–1909).

Theodor Duka was a Tibetologist and linguist. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and St George's, University of London. He served as an assistant surgeon and Surgeon-Lieutenant-Colonel in the Bengal Army (1854–1874) and was Vice-President of the British and Foreign Bible Society.

Theodor Goldstücker was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Königsberg and studied at Bonn. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London and the University of London (1851–1872), and was president of the Philological Society (~1871–1872).

Theodor Korsch was a linguist and Indologist who earned his candidate's degree, master's, and PhD at Moscow State University. He served as Privatdozent (1868) and extraordinary professor (1883–1905) at Moscow State University, and also held posts at Odesa University and the Lazarev Institute.

Theodor Mommsen was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the Christianeum and Kiel University. He held positions at the universities of Leipzig, Zurich, Breslau, and Frederick William University Berlin (1861–1885), and at the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1858).

Theodor Nöldeke specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. After earning his PhD and habilitating at Göttingen, he worked at the Royal Library of Berlin and held professorships at Göttingen, Kiel (1864–1872), and Strasbourg (1872–1906).
Theodor Schultze worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied law at Kiel University (~1843–1847) and also studied at Frederick William University Berlin.

Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen (PhD), and Oxford, and habilitated at Greifswald. He served as Privatdozent and professor at Greifswald before becoming professor of comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).
Theodor von Oppolzer studied at the University of Vienna (~1859–1865) and subsequently held a post there from around 1866 to 1886.

Theodore Dwight Woolsey was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at Hopkins School, Yale, and Princeton. He served as president of Yale University (1831–1871) and as president of the American Oriental Society (~1856–1860).

Theodore Riccardi worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 1974–1976 and 1990) and served as a guest editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society in 1989.
Theodore Riccardi Jr. is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He has held faculty posts at Columbia University, where he is attested as faculty in 2014 and Professor Emeritus in 2026.

Theodore Stcherbatsky worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi, and was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1927–1931).
Theodorus Christiaan Vriezen was a scholar of religious studies who held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1941–1956) and Utrecht University (1956–1969).
